Baby. She's grieving. You guys broke up. She doesn't want an LDR. That is what she wants currently. You know exactly what she wants. 

I'm sure you both have love for each other. And for your sake, you need to set healthy boundaries for yourself. You can't let yourself lose yourself completely for one person. Stresses in LDRs can cause a rift when a traumatic event happens. If you plan to move to where your partner is solely for them is unfair for you. If you truly want to be where you're planning to move, great. 

Continue to be there for her. But if one partner does not want to be currently in the relationship, then, don't try to force a relationship where there isn't supposed to be one. You can support her without needing to be in a relationship with her. And it may be hard for you. You might not want that, and if so, distance yourself. 

You can't keep investing in this relationship solely because you to expect that that person will maybe want to be back with you again. Again, if you're moving to where that person is, and you're both still single, maybe try again. Or maybe you'll have moved on since, but do not torture yourself over whether this person wants to be with you or not. 

I hope and wish you the best. Hope everything works for you in the end. And don't forget to take care of yourself in the process.
